findings.statement: Benchmark posts claim AMD MI300X provides 2.4× more memory capacity and 1.6× higher bandwidth than Nvidia H100, highlighting a perceived performance advantage for AMD among some AI developers.
limitations: Based on a single social‑post on X; limited language coverage (English/Korean) and no corroborating sources.

findings.statement: NVIDIA promotes its A100 Tensor Core GPU as delivering up to 20× higher performance over the prior generation, reflecting strong positive messaging about performance among cloud providers.
limitations: Single web‑based marketing page; no independent validation in the sample.

findings.statement: Vultr announced a 20 MW AMD AI supercluster deployment in India, indicating significant adoption of AMD GPUs by a cloud service provider.
limitations: Both items are news articles focused on an Indian deployment; no evidence of similar AMD deployments in the US or Europe.

findings.statement: NVIDIA A100 GPUs are listed for up to $22,000 on retail sites, suggesting high acquisition cost that may deter some cloud operators or AI developers.
limitations: Price shown on a retail listing; does not reflect negotiated cloud‑service pricing.

findings.statement: Fireworks AI states that it offers Llama inference using both Nvidia and AMD GPUs, suggesting developers view both vendors as viable for inference workloads.
limitations: Both sources are social‑media posts on X; no quantitative performance or cost data provided.
